claim: ABHD10 is an S-depalmitoylase acting on PRDX5
key_finding: Human ABHD10 identified as a resident mitochondrial APT-family S-depalmitoylase; PRDX5 is a substrate and ABHD10 regulates palmitoylation of the PRDX5 nucleophilic active-site cysteine
context: Human cells (HEK293T/HeLa), chemoproteomic and activity-probe assays
confidence: High for human; no zebrafish assay exists, so transfer to either zebrafish paralog is by orthology

citation: PDB 6NY9 (DOI:10.2210/pdb6NY9/pdb); structure used in this run
claim: The acyl-binding channel of ABHD10 can be defined and its lining residues cross-mapped to the zebrafish paralogs
key_finding: Mouse ABHD10 (Q6PE15) at 1.66 A, chain B residues 1-250, offset +43. Geometric triad detection (Ser OG to His NE2 2.87 A; Asp OD to His ND1 < 3.6 A) gives Ser100-Asp197-His227 PDB = mouse Ser143-Asp240-His270, matching UniProt human active sites 152/249/279 exactly. LIGSITE-style cavity detection (psp >= 13 core 23 A^3; psp >= 12 within 13 A, channel 134 A^3) yields 27 lining residues
context: Mouse protein, crystal structure; no ligand-bound ABHD10 structure exists
confidence: Moderate-high for channel geometry; apo structure, so the acyl chain path is inferred from cavity shape

claim: The paralogs are similar enough that divergence must be argued from specific residues
key_finding: abhd10b vs abhd10a 71.9% identity; abhd10b vs human ABHD10 66.4%; abhd10a vs human 65.9%. Neither zebrafish copy is detectably closer to human
confidence: High; global alignment of unambiguous sequences

claim: Both paralogs retain the complete triad and oxyanion loop; channel differences exist
key_finding: abhd10b Ser136-Asp233-His263 and abhd10a Ser131-Asp228-His258 both complete, both oxyanion-hole backbone amide donors present. 19 of 27 lining residues identical; 8 differ (a>b): F63>Y68, L76>G69 equivalent, I193F>I198, H188>S193, R259>H264, L196>V201, H66>N71, Q70>P75. Net channel volume 230 A^3 smaller in abhd10b by residue-volume accounting
context: Sequence cross-map onto the 6NY9 cavity; no zebrafish structure
confidence: Moderate; volume change is a residue-volume estimate, not a modelled cavity

claim: The channel differences sit at functionally constrained positions
key_finding: Across 26 single-copy tetrapod orthologs, the 8 differing positions have mean entropy 1.643 bits vs 0.710 bits at the 19 agreeing positions (Mann-Whitney one-sided p = 0.0047). None of the 8 is invariant; 7 of 19 agreeing positions are invariant. abhd10b and abhd10a each match the tetrapod consensus at 18 of 27 positions; among the 8 differing positions each is ancestral at 2
context: UniProt ortholog panel, mammals to amphibians, 60.2-100% identity to human
confidence: High; the comparison is internal to one alignment set and the effect is symmetric between paralogs

claim: One paralog is relaxed and the other constrained after the duplication
key_finding: Tajima relative-rate test against five single-copy outgroups gives p = 0.23 to 0.86 (chi-square, 1 df); no outgroup shows asymmetry. Protein dN differs by under 6% between the copies and the direction is inconsistent across outgroups. dN/dS is not computable: synonymous sites are saturated at pS 0.74-0.88
context: Protein-level RRT plus Nei-Gojobori counting on CDS
confidence: Moderate; the test has limited power at this divergence and saturation blocks the codon-model version

citation: This run: PRDX5 cross-map; PMID:31740833 for the substrate site
claim: Substrate duplication state bears on partitioning
key_finding: Zebrafish has a single prdx5 gene. The human PRDX5 peroxidatic Cys100 aligns to zebrafish Cys47 (mature-protein numbering differences aside) inside a 17/17 identical sequence window
context: UniProt and Ensembl zebrafish gene set
confidence: High for single-copy status and site conservation; no zebrafish palmitoylation data

claim: Ohnolog retention is the exception, so a retained pair invites a divergence reading
key_finding: Loss of one duplicate is the most common fate after teleost genome duplication, at roughly 80%
confidence: Review-level orientation; it motivates the hypothesis but does not test it

claim: abhd10a and abhd10b are TGD ohnologs rather than a tandem or lineage-specific duplication
key_finding: Three double-conserved syntenic families within +/- 1.2 Mb: tagln3a/tagln3b, gtf3aa/gtf3ab, wasf3a/wasf3b. Human ABHD10-TAGLN3-TMPRSS7 block retained in both copies. Ensembl Compara calls human ABHD10 ortholog_one2many to exactly these two genes

claim: Expression partitioning could distinguish subfunctionalization from redundancy
key_finding: Ensembl has no abhd10b gene on primary chr24. The 289-aa abhd10b ORF is transcript tagln3b-201 (ENSDART00000113092) of gene ENSDARG00000058394, displayed as tagln3b. Coding exons of the two transcript sets do not overlap; the merge rests on a 583 bp UTR overlap at 21,923,348-21,923,930. NCBI keeps them separate (abhd10b GeneID 492622, tagln3b GeneID 797861). Expression Atlas returned HTTP 404 and Bgee HTTP 403 in this environment
confidence: High for the model defect; no expression numbers obtained, and none are reported

claim: Mitochondrial localization is retained in both copies
key_finding: abhd10b N-terminal 45 residues: 6 basic, 0 acidic, net +6, 5 Ser/Thr, max 18-residue amphipathic moment 1.06, matching human (+6, 1.11), mouse (+8, 0.84) and Xenopus (+7, 1.24). abhd10a has two annotated starts: A0A0R4ILM1 net +1 with 6 acidic residues (not presequence-like) and A0A8M2BCX5 net +6, 9 Ser/Thr, moment 1.42
context: Sequence feature calculation; UniProt annotates a 1-52 transit peptide on human ABHD10
confidence: High for abhd10b; unresolved for abhd10a because of the 5' start ambiguity

claim: Public ortholog sets can be used directly for rate tests
key_finding: Spotted gar ENSLOCP00000005329 has lost the nucleophile elbow to a mis-predicted exon and chicken ENSGALP00010006097 aligns at 17.5-27.8% to all other ABHD10s. Both were excluded; four other single-copy outgroups were used
confidence: High; both are clear model defects, not biology
